newsitem.title: USA: New Jersey teen says she did not kill her baby.
newsitem.headline: New Jersey teen says she did not kill her baby.

text.p: A New Jersey teenager accused of killing her newborn son maintained her innocence in a television interview to be broadcast Friday and said she was terrified at the prospect of the death penalty.

"I would never hurt anything or anybody, especially something that would come from me," Amy Grossberg said in the interview with ABC television journalist Barbara Walters to be broadcast Friday evening on the ABC News programme "20/20". A transcript was provided in advance by the network.

Grossberg and the boy's father, Brian Peterson, both 18, were arrested in November and charged with killing the baby shortly after Grossberg gave birth in a Delaware motel room. Authorities say the boy was hit in the head and his body was stuffed in a plastic bag, which was found in a trash bin the next day.

An autopsy showed the boy was born alive and died of severe skull fractures. A later medical examiner's report said the baby had a brain defect unrelated to the death and lawyers for the two argue the baby may have been unable to survive.

Grossberg and Peterson, who were childhood sweethearts attending separate colleges at the time of the birth, pleaded innocent to the charges, which included first-degree murder. They were released on bail in January and allowed to return to their homes in northern New Jersey pending trial.
Delaware Attorney General Jane Brady said the two could face the death penalty if convicted.

Asked how she felt about a death sentence, Grossberg said: "Just hearing those words are terrifying." She said she had been in love with Peterson, with thoughts of marriage, and denied speculation she would turn against him in court.
"Brian and I have a really good relationship. I care for him a lot ... And that will stay the same."
She said she had visited the grave of her son and mourned the loss. "It was a part of me. My heart breaks," she said.

Grossberg's mother, Sonye Grossberg, said she saw Amy two weeks before the birth and had no idea she was pregnant. She said she believed she knew why Amy hid her pregnancy but was prevented by a court-imposed gag order from discussing it.

Prosecutors have said they would review the interview to see whether it violated the gag order. Peterson's attorney, Joseph Hurley, told Philadelphia ABC affiliate WPVI his client had no plans to grant a similar interview but that could change depending on the response to the Grossberg interview.
